fish.name: Coral Nibbler
fish.flavor: Spends all day gumming the coral like a toddler with a biscuit. The reef has learned to put up with it.

fish.name: Tidepool Goby
fish.flavor: Lives in a puddle and considers it a kingdom. Honestly, good for him.

fish.name: Sandy Wrasse
fish.flavor: Sleeps buried in the sand with just its lips poking out. Locals call that 'the full weekend'.

fish.name: Lagoon Mullet
fish.flavor: Travels in gangs of forty and panics in perfect unison. A very organized way to be nervous.

fish.name: Penny Damsel
fish.flavor: Small, blue, and furious about it. Will defend a fist-sized patch of algae to the bitter end.

fish.name: Sergeant Minor
fish.flavor: Wears five crisp stripes and salutes nobody. Demoted from Sergeant Major for eating the parade.

fish.name: Reef Sprat
fish.flavor: The reef's most popular fish, in the sense that everything wants to eat it. It copes by being extremely fast and a little bit smug.

fish.name: Blushing Blenny
fish.flavor: Goes pink whenever you make eye contact. Scientists insist it's camouflage; the blenny knows the truth.

fish.name: Pebble Puffer
fish.flavor: Inflates into a perfect little stone when startled, which is often. Deflates with a long, dignified squeak.

fish.name: Dozing Sweetlips
fish.flavor: Sleeps twenty hours a day under the same ledge, lips gently puckered. The reef's most reliable landmark.

fish.name: Cove Cardinal
fish.flavor: Carries its eggs in its mouth and its opinions nowhere. Comes out at dusk looking faintly embarrassed.

fish.name: Skipping Halfbeak
fish.flavor: Skims the surface on its tail like a thrown stone that refuses to sink. Nobody taught it this; it just believes.

fish.name: Sunny Chromis
fish.flavor: A flake of green light with fins. Catch one and your whole hand smells faintly of summer.

fish.name: Whiskered Goatfish
fish.flavor: Sweeps the sand with two chin whiskers like a fussy little groundskeeper. Finds everything except peace.

fish.name: Tideline Silverside
fish.flavor: Arrives with the tide, leaves with the tide, remembers nothing in between. An enviable schedule.

fish.name: Grandma's Grunt
fish.flavor: Makes a low grumbling noise when handled, exactly like Grandma Posy getting out of her chair. Named with love.

fish.name: Gossip Parrotfish
fish.flavor: Crunches coral all day and mutters constantly through its beak. Whatever it's saying, the wrasses seem scandalized.

fish.name: Porcupine Puffball
fish.flavor: A ball of spikes with the eyes of an apologetic dog. It's very sorry about the spikes. They're staying, though.

fish.name: Old Rope Moray
fish.flavor: Looks exactly like a frayed hawser until it yawns. Fishers here shake every rope twice, just in case.

fish.name: Sneaky Trumpeter
fish.flavor: Hangs vertically among the sea whips pretending to be scenery. It is not scenery. It is watching you.

fish.name: Latchkey Lionfish
fish.flavor: Drifts home to the same coral head at dusk, fins trailing like a coat too fancy for the weather. Do not pat it.

fish.name: Cobblestone Boxfish
fish.flavor: A small armored cube that steers like a shopping trolley. Bumps into things, apologizes with a puff, carries on.

fish.name: Carpet Flounder
fish.flavor: Flat as a doormat and twice as patient. Has been lying on the same patch of sand since before you were born, probably.

fish.name: Big-Eye Squirrelfish
fish.flavor: Eyes like polished saucers, tuned for midnight. Spends the day under a ledge judging everyone's technique.

fish.name: Grumpy Triggerfish
fish.flavor: Guards a circle of sand nobody else wants and bites anyone who forgets. The circle moves. The grudge doesn't.

fish.name: Tattletale Filefish
fish.flavor: Covered head to tail in scribbly lines, like someone's diary got loose. Reads suspiciously like yours.

fish.name: One-Horn Wanda
fish.flavor: Every unicornfish has a horn; Wanda has a horn with a story. She lost the tip to a crab pot in '58 and has out-swum every net since.

fish.name: Moonlit Mandarin
fish.flavor: Painted in swirls no honest brush could manage, and only comes out when the moon is on the water. Blink slowly, or you'll miss the whole performance.

fish.name: Postmaster Grouper
fish.flavor: Swallowed a mailbag off the ferry dock in living memory, and folk swear he still delivers. Letters lost at sea have a way of washing up near his hole, dry as a bone.

fish.name: Bride's Veil Angel
fish.flavor: Trails white fins so long and fine they snag on the coral like lace. The story says she's been circling the cove since a wedding that never happened.

fish.name: Whistling Cowfish
fish.flavor: A horned little box that hums a two-note tune as it putters along. Old-timers say it learned the melody from a lighthouse keeper who whistled at his work.

fish.name: Lantern-Jaw Jack
fish.flavor: Comes tearing through the shallows at first light with his underbite leading the charge. The sprats have a word for him, and it isn't printable.

fish.name: Copperbelly Snapper
fish.flavor: Its belly gleams like a pan hung in a sunlit kitchen. Caught once a season, talked about all year.

fish.name: The Coral Warden
fish.flavor: An ancient grouper grown so crusted with polyps that the reef considers him a district. Where he settles, the coral blooms; where he glares, the anchors drag up empty.

fish.name: Grandfather Tide
fish.flavor: A parrotfish older than the harbor, whose beak has ground whole reefs into the white sand you're standing on. Every beach in the cove is, technically, his life's work.

fish.name: Mother-of-Pearl Matron
fish.flavor: Her scales carry the same slow shine as the inside of an oyster, and the light never sits still on her. Divers surface from her wake speaking softly for days.

fish.name: The Anemone Bride
fish.flavor: She wears a crown of living anemones and the reef's stinging things part around her like courtiers. Take the catch photo quickly and put her back politely.

fish.name: The Reef That Swims
fish.flavor: Once a generation, a stretch of coral stands up, shakes off its fish, and goes for a wander. It carries a whole neighborhood on its back, and the neighborhood has opinions about your hook.

fish.name: The Chapel Bellringer
fish.flavor: A drowned chapel sits at the cove's deep edge, and on still nights its bell rings true. Beneath it circles a great silver fish, striking the hour with its tail, keeping a promise no one alive remembers making.

fish.name: The First Color
fish.flavor: Before this cove, the old folk say, the sea was grey; then one fish swam through and everything it touched forgot how to be dull. Hold your line steady. Every color you have ever loved is looking back at you.
